overall: Tomorrow (Saturday, June 27) in Los Angeles is expected to be a mild, partly sunny day with patchy morning coastal fog clearing by mid-morning, giving way to filtered sunshine in the afternoon. A persistent south to south-southwest onshore flow of 5–10 mph (gusts to 20 mph) will keep the marine layer influence active, suppressing temperatures well below seasonal norms. No tropical or severe weather is expected for the LA coast; the active wind advisories are confined to far inland desert and mountain areas (Inyo County, Owens Valley, Mohave County, AZ) and pose no direct impact.
forecast_obs_notes: Model agreement is notably poor and spread wide: GFS is a significant warm outlier (~84°F), NBM anchors the cool end (~68.3°F) in line with the NWS official text forecast of near 70°F, while ECMWF (~76°F), HRRR (~77.8°F), and Weather.com (~75°F) cluster in the mid-70s. This multi-model divergence of ~16°F between GFS and NBM reflects genuine uncertainty and is the primary driver of a flat, diffuse ensemble probability distribution.
max_temp_prediction: The ensemble model expects a TMAX near 75°F, meaningfully above the NWS official call of ~70°F, with the prior-day observed high of 71.6°F providing a useful anchor under similar coastal-fog conditions. The probability distribution is extremely flat — five consecutive 2-degree buckets from 70–79°F each carry roughly 20% probability — yielding Tier 4 (Poor) signal quality on both even and odd bucket sets with just 32% expected accuracy; this is a market to avoid. Best single estimate is approximately 73–75°F, with high uncertainty skewed slightly warmer by GFS and HRRR but tempered by the marine layer and NWS/NBM cool bias.
